pull.title: docs: bring the Guide, Get Started and the reference docs up to 6.39.0
pull.body:
## What this is

The documentation release for the 6.22.0 → 6.39.0 arc.

Going in, the assumption was that all four surfaces had fallen behind. They had
not. `README.md`, `docs/USAGE.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` were updated release by
release across the arc and are, on inspection, accurate and current — USAGE
already documents the `quota` billing phrases with a measured example, the
Qwen/Pi user-agent collision, `--skip-trust`, `--no-gitignore` and every
harness. **The in-dashboard Guide is what had fallen behind**, and the Guide is
where a user is standing when they need help. So this PR is weighted there, and
it deliberately does not rewrite prose that was already right.

## Doc sections added or rewritten

### `src/my_claude_code/api/admin_static/index.html` — the Guide

| Section | Heading | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#guide-walkthrough` | First run, end to end | **new** |
| `#guide-agent-tiers` | Tiers for every agent | **new** |
| `#guide-attribution` | Which agent sent this? | **new** |
| `#guide-credits` | When a provider runs out of credit | **new** |

All four are wired into the Guide's table of contents.

### `src/my_claude_code/config/onboarding.py` — Get Started

- New optional step **"Launch a coding agent"**, pointing at the Coding agents
  page — which has existed since 6.23.0 while the checklist still described a
  single-client world.
- "Connect a model provider" now also names **Add custom provider** as the
  route for an endpoint MCC does not already know.
- "Set your fallback model" now names both tier families: the Claude aliases
  for Claude Code, and `mcc/best|good|medium|cheap|vision` for every other
  agent.

### `src/my_claude_code/api/admin_static/admin.js`

Marking an onboarding step visited stops being a hardcoded special case for
`guide` and becomes what every step does. The server already decides which
steps are visit-based; the page should not carry a second copy of that list.

### `ARCHITECTURE.md`

| Section | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `### Catalogue File Materialisation` | **new** |
| `### Harness Attribution` | **new** |
| `### The Anthropic Subscription Client Gate` | **new** |

The existing `Coding-Agent Tier Aliases`, `Custom Providers`, `Upstream
Recovery Ladder`, `The Harness Registry` and `Capability To Catalogue Mapping`
sections were already present and correct, and are untouched.

### `README.md`

Two factual corrections, both found by the new drift guard (below). No
restructuring — the provider table already carries HyperCharm, and the three
inbound surfaces already have connect-your-client recipes.

### `docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`

§4 rewritten. The stale-PNG list is **empty**, with one documented exception.
It now carries the scratch-instance capture recipe (fake keys, `VACUUM INTO`
log copy, read-only models.dev cache, `PORT=8199 HOST=127.0.0.1`) and the two
rules that have each broken a release: a screenshot lives in **two**
directories, and no secret may be legible **even truncated**.

## The drift guard

`tests/contracts/test_docs_reference_drift.py`, with
`tests/contracts/docs_reference_allowlist.txt` for names the docs mention on
purpose. It checks that every environment variable, `mcc-*`/`fcc-*` command,
HTTP route and dashboard page name used in code voice in README, USAGE and the
Guide actually resolves — against `Settings.model_fields`, the websearch
catalogue, the harness/launcher/catalogue modules, `[project.scripts]` **and**
`[project.gui-scripts]`, the route decorators plus the `wire_surfaces`
constants, and `VIEW_GROUPS`.

**What it caught on the first run.**

Two real drifts in `README.md`, both of which would have made a reader's edit
do nothing:

1. "match the API key to `AUTH_TOKEN`" — the setting is
   **`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`**.
2. "`MAX_CONCURRENCY` moved here" — the field is
   **`PROVIDER_MAX_CONCURRENCY`**.

Four blind spots in the guard itself, each fixed rather than excused:

3. `mcc-desktop` reported missing — it lives in `[project.gui-scripts]`, which
   the first version did not read.
4. `mcc-backup`, `fcc-backup`, `mcc-harness` reported as missing launchers —
   they are the `.mcc-backup` file suffix and the `x-mcc-harness` header. The
   command pattern now refuses a match preceded by `.` or `-`.
5. `BRAVE_COUNTRY` and ~20 siblings reported as nonexistent — search settings
   live in the websearch catalogue, not `Settings`. `GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING`,
   `KIMI_CODE_HOME` and friends likewise live in the launchers and catalogue
   serialisers, not `config/harnesses.py`.
6. `docs/USAGE.md` "from the **Limits** tab in 5.48.0" flagged as a missing
   page. It is a true sentence about a page since renamed **Limits &
   Resilience**; the guard now only fails *instructions*, not history.

A companion test fails if an allow-list entry becomes real, so the file cannot
quietly rot — it immediately retired seven entries once the scan widened.

Everything else the guard flagged was triaged against source and is a
deliberate mention: other tools' variables (`CLOUD_CODE_URL`,
`GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE`, `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY`, `NIM_ENABLE_KV_CACHE_REUSE`,
`UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR`, Qwen's own `DEFAULT_TOKEN_LIMIT`), two settings documented as
**removed** (`CREDENTIAL_CIRCUIT_THRESHOLD`, `MIN_CREDENTIAL_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS`),
a variable USAGE names precisely to say it does **not** exist (`KIMI_CODE_HOME`),
and upstream error phrases quoted so a log line can be matched (`LOCKED_OUT`,
`NOT_ENOUGH_BALANCE`).

## Screenshots

Captured from an **isolated scratch instance** on `127.0.0.1:8199` — never the
live `:8082`, which was only ever read. The scratch `HOME` was built from the
*shape* of a real install: every secret replaced with a fake of the same shape,
a `VACUUM INTO` copy of the request log (272,592 requests, so the pages show
real-looking data), and the `models.dev` cache copied read-only so the ladder
resolves offline. Each file is written to **both** `assets/` and
`src/my_claude_code/api/admin_static/img/`.

**New:** `admin-get-started.png` (the checklist and its progress),
`admin-providers.png` (57 providers, 13 configured, keys shown only as counts),
`admin-custom-provider.png` (base URL, key pool, Refresh models),
`admin-models.png` (per-model sources and tier chips),
`admin-coding-agents.png` (all 16 harnesses; Antigravity marked not servable),
`admin-coding-agent-card.png` (one card's commands, generated file, tiers),
`admin-analytics-harness.png` (the harness column, filter and breakdown).

**Refreshed:** `admin-page`, `admin-version`, `admin-requests`,
`admin-key-performance`, `admin-websearch`, `admin-websearch-analytics`,
`admin-messaging`, `admin-model-config`, `admin-models-bulk`, `admin-analytics`,
`admin-request-detail`, `admin-request-contradiction`, `admin-limits`,
`admin-limits-calculator`, `admin-credential-health`.

**Not refreshed, and said so in the checklist:** `assets/admin-update-banner.png`.
The banner only renders when a newer release exists, which an offline scratch
instance running the version under development cannot produce. Not fabricated.

**Secret scan, and what it caught.** The rule for this release is that no
published screenshot may show an `sk-` prefix *at all*, masked or not, because
a masked label still carries a real key's first and last characters.

Two separate violations were found and fixed, both by looking at the images
rather than trusting the capture:

1. The **previous, committed** `admin-request-detail.png` rendered a key label
   reading `sk-n…oKuN`. It had shipped that way. Its replacement shows
   `user…ubCk`.
2. The **first re-capture** of `admin-key-performance.png` rendered five real
   masked labels — `sk-n…0awp`, `sk-n…oKuN`, `sk-8…Kofx`, `sk-o…7e52`,
   `sk-2…otqn`. Faking the keys in the scratch `.env` was not enough: the
   copied request log still carried `key_label` values captured from real
   traffic. Fixed at the source by rewriting every `sk-…` label in the scratch
   database — five distinct labels, mapped 1:1 across `requests`,
   `request_attempts` and the three rollup tables so the aggregates still add
   up — and re-capturing.

No `sk-` byte sequence appears in any of the 56 PNGs, and the scratch data they
were rendered from now serves zero `sk-` key labels. No screenshot shows a
request or response body; the one body-adjacent panel captured is MCC's own
"REQUEST BODY SENT (NO PROMPT TEXT)", which renders structural fields and
character counts only.

## Verification

- `uv run ruff format --check` — clean, repo-wide.
- `uv run ruff check src/ tests/` — All checks passed.
- `uv run ty check src/ tests/` — All checks passed.
- `pytest` (redirected `HOME`): **8977 passed, 38 skipped, 14 failed** — the
  known local baseline (PowerShell installer tests, websearch registry/settings,
  two web-tool tests). None are in code this PR touches.
- `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py -n 0`: **219 passed**.
- `tests/contracts/`: **401 passed**, including `test_admin_asset_wiring.py`,
  `test_admin_models_view.py`, the Guide and XSS contract tests, and
  `test_feature_manifest`.
- `tests/contracts/test_docs_reference_drift.py`: **13 passed**.
- Onboarding: **32 passed** after updating the three tests that pin the step
  list. `test_every_step_view_is_a_known_dashboard_view` now derives its view
  set from `VIEW_GROUPS` instead of a hand-kept list that had already fallen
  four views behind.
- Guide markup: parsed and checked for balance; all four new anchors resolve
  from the TOC; every image the Guide references exists in both directories.

## Residual risks

- **Prose accuracy is still unguarded.** The new test proves every identifier
  resolves; it cannot prove a sentence is true. The four new Guide sections
  were each written against the source (`core/tier_refs.py`,
  `config/harness_tiers.py`, `core/client_fingerprint.py`,
  `providers/anthropic_oauth/entrypoint.py`, `core/failures.py`,
  `config/settings.py`) rather than from release notes.
- **Screenshots carry scratch-instance cosmetics.** The sticky action bar shows
  a `C:\tmp\claude\…` config path in some full-page captures, and one full-page
  shot is very tall. Cosmetic only; no secret and no user content.
- **`admin-update-banner.png` remains pre-6.x.** Documented, not hidden — the
  banner only renders when a newer release exists, which an instance running
  the version under development cannot produce.
- **New Guide image filenames 404 on an already-running server.**
  `_bundled_image_names()` (`api/admin_routes.py:364`) is `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`,
  so the servable-PNG allowlist is snapshotted once per process. Verified: the
  two newly named images 404'd on the running scratch server and all eight
  returned 200 after a restart. This is a **dev-time gotcha only** — an install
  of this release starts a fresh process — so the cache is deliberately left
  alone in a documentation PR, and is recorded here rather than fixed.
- **The drift guard only reads code voice** — backticks and fenced blocks. A
  variable named in plain prose is not checked, deliberately, because
  instructions are formatted and prose mentions are where the false positives
  live.
- The one PowerShell-installer and websearch baseline failures are unrelated
  and pre-existing; this PR touches neither installer scripts nor websearch.

commit.message:
docs: bring the Guide, Get Started and the reference docs up to 6.39.0

The 6.22.0-6.39.0 arc added custom-provider parity, the harness registry and
its fourteen launchers, three inbound protocol surfaces, per-harness tiers,
harness attribution and the universal recovery nets. README.md, docs/USAGE.md
and ARCHITECTURE.md had largely kept pace release by release. The in-dashboard
Guide had not, and the Guide is where a user actually is when they need it.

The Guide gains a real first-run walkthrough -- install, start, dashboard, add
a provider by key or by base URL, read the Models page, set the tiers, launch
an agent, find the request in Analytics -- and the three sections it was
missing outright: what the five `mcc/*` tier aliases point at and what happens
to a tier you leave unset, how a request gets attributed to a coding agent and
why Qwen Code and Pi are filed as Claude Code until they send the header, and
why running out of credits does not end a route.

Get Started grows a Coding agents step. That page has existed since 6.23.0 and
is how every non-Claude CLI is launched, but the checklist still described a
world with one client in it. Marking a step visited stops being a special case
for the Guide and becomes something every step does, which is what let the new
step exist at all.

ARCHITECTURE.md gains the three layers it had no section for: catalogue file
materialisation (the server writes, the launcher only reads, and why the
pre-6.36.1 ordering failed permanently), harness attribution and its one
irreducible user-agent collision, and the Anthropic subscription client gate --
including that the gate reads a good-faith attribution field and is not an
authenticator.

A new contract test closes the mechanical half of the standing "docs drift is
unguarded" item. It checks that every environment variable, `mcc-*` command,
HTTP route and dashboard page name the docs use in code voice actually
resolves, with an allow-list for names mentioned on purpose -- another tool's
variable, a setting documented as removed. It found two real drifts on its
first run: README told the reader to set `AUTH_TOKEN` when the setting is
`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, and named `MAX_CONCURRENCY` when the field is
`PROVIDER_MAX_CONCURRENCY`. Both are edits a reader would have made to no
effect. It also found four of its own blind spots, each now covered rather than
excused.

Every dashboard screenshot is re-captured against an isolated scratch instance
built from the shape of a real install with fake keys and a VACUUM INTO copy of
the request log, so the pages show real-looking data and no secret. The
previous `admin-request-detail.png` rendered a key label reading `sk-n...oKuN`;
no published screenshot shows an `sk-` prefix now, and the release checklist
says to check for it.
